data.gender_notes: Priya is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root prī, 'to please, to love' — priya, 'beloved, dear'. Its root is Sanskrit prī (प्री). A classical Sanskrit term of endearment. Priya is a Sanskrit name meaning “Beloved; dear; pleasing”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Priya total 33, reducing to 6. Number 6 is associated with responsibility, care and harmony.

vedic_reference.note: The name Priya is derived from the Sanskrit word प्रिय (priya), which means 'beloved', 'dear', or 'precious'. It is a popular name in Hinduism and is used in various religious texts and mythologies. For instance, Priya is the name of the wife of the sage Veda Vyasa, who is the author of the Mahabharata. Priya is also mentioned in the Bhagavad Gita, where Lord Krishna speaks about the importance of loving and serving the divine.
